rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arab formulations such as killing is safest from killing are rhetorically weaker: they make a thing cause its own absence, repeat killing, narrow the point, and fail for unjust killing.
rows.anchor: وقالت العرب فيما يقرب من هذا المعنى: القتل أوقى للقتل، وقالوا: أنفى للقتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Retaliatory killing produces a particular kind of life, not life in general; alternatively, supply an omitted noun so the law of retaliation is what causes life.
rows.anchor: نوعا من القتل وهو القصاص سبب لنوع من أنواع الحياة، لا لمطلق الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾānic wording is smoother and more beautiful than the Arab saying: it avoids repeating the word killing and needs no omitted comparison such as safer than abandoning killing.
rows.anchor: لعذوبة الألفاظ وحسن التركيب وعدم الاحتياج إلى تقدير الحذف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Retaliation is broader than killing because it applies to offenses against life and other injuries, so the verse is more comprehensive and better secures life.
rows.anchor: القصاص أعم من القتل، لأن القصاص يكون في نفس وفي غير نفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Retaliation signals deserved punishment, so establishing it leads to life.
rows.anchor: فلأن القصاص مشعر بالاستحقاق، فترتب على مشروعيته وجود الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse sets retaliation against life, an antithesis called ṭibāq, like the cited pairing of giving death and life.
rows.anchor: فيها مقابلة القصاص بالحياة فهو من مقابلة الشيء بضده، وهو نوع من البيان يسمى الطباق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence has a subject and predicate; the phrase in retaliation is attached to what governs for you and placed as predicate, allowing an indefinite subject to begin the sentence.
rows.anchor: وهذه الجملة مبتدأ وخبر، وفي القصاص: متعلق بما تعلق به قوله: لكم، وهو في موضع الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address calls rational, perceptive people to recognize the public benefit of retaliation; they understand consequences and danger, whereas those without reason do not attain fear.
rows.anchor: ونبه بالنداء نداء ذوي العقول والبصائر على المصلحة العامة، وهي مشروعية القصاص

rows.speaker: قول غير مسمى
rows.claim: The phrase is explained as avoiding murder, fearing retaliation or becoming engrossed in killing, fearing God by avoiding sins, or acting piously by upholding and applying retaliation.
rows.anchor: لعلكم تتقون أي: القصاص، فتكفون عن القتل وتتقون القتل حذرا من القصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first explanation, that the verse establishes retaliation, is the purpose for which the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: أولاها ما سيقت له الآية من مشروعية القصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The will verse follows naturally after the discussion of killing, retaliation, and blood money: it alerts each person to make a will before sudden death.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنه لما ذكر تعالى القتل في القصاص، والدية، أتبع ذلك بالتنبيه على الوصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no need to coordinate this clause with the earlier command about retaliation or posit a deleted conjunction; it is a new sentence clearly connected in meaning to what precedes.
rows.anchor: ولا ضرورة تدعو إلى أن: كتب، أصله: العطف على. كتب عليكم القصاص في القتلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author's preferred sense of death's arrival is the arrival of its precursors and causes, such as illness and alarming symptoms; Arabic usage metaphorically calls causes of death death.
rows.anchor: ومعنى حضور الموت أي: حضور مقدماته وأسبابه من العلل والأمراض والأعراض المخوفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾānic phrase about death coming from every place while the person is not dead and the cited poems use death for its causes or personify death; Antarah, Jarir, and an unnamed poet provide examples.
rows.anchor: والعرب تطلق على أسباب الموت موتا على سبيل التجوز. وقال تعالى: ويأتيه الموت من كل مكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural address means each believer individually, then the clause switches to one of you; the expected plural was avoided by following the universal sense of upon you, a rare construction illustrated by poetry.
rows.anchor: ولو جرى نظم الكلام على خطاب المؤمنين لكان: إذا حضركم الموت، لكنه روعيت دلالة العموم في: عليكم

rows.speaker: قول غير مسمى
rows.claim: An alternative takes death literally and addresses executors and heirs: when someone dies they must carry out the will; on this reading the verse itself does not prove that making a will is obligatory.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المراد بالموت هنا حقيقته لا مقدماته، فيكون الخطاب متوجها إلى الأوصياء والورثة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says khayr means wealth throughout the Qurʾān, citing its uses for wealth in several other passages.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: الخير في القرآن كله المال وإنه لحب الخير لشديد

rows.speaker: الزهري وأبو مجلز
rows.claim: They take the apparent wording to mean any amount of wealth, so a will is due whether the estate is small or large.
rows.anchor: وبه قال: الزهري، وأبو مجلز، وغيرهما، قالوا: تجب فيما قل وفيما كثر

rows.speaker: أبان
rows.claim: Aban sets the minimum estate for the obligation at two hundred silver dirhams.
rows.anchor: وقال أبان: مائتا درهم فضة

rows.speaker: النخعي
rows.claim: Al-Nakhaʿi places the threshold between one thousand and five hundred dirhams.
rows.anchor: وقال النخعي: من ألف درهم إلى خمسمائة

rows.speaker: علي وقتادة
rows.claim: ʿAli and Qatada set the threshold at one thousand dirhams or more.
rows.anchor: وقال علي: وقتادة: ألف درهم فصاعدا

rows.speaker: الجصاص
rows.claim: Al-Jaṣṣāṣ sets the threshold at four thousand dirhams.
rows.anchor: وقال الجصاص: أربعة آلاف درهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who define sufficient wealth by its relative abundance say the amount depends on a person's circumstances and the number of dependents.
rows.anchor: وأما من قدره بمطلق الكثرة، فإن ذلك يختلف بحسب اختلاف حال الرجل، وكثرة عياله

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿĀʾisha considered four hundred dinars no surplus for a man with dependents; for a family of four and three thousand, she likewise called it little and advised leaving it to the children.
rows.anchor: وروي عن عائشة أنها قالت: ما أرى فضلا في مال هو أربعمائة دينار لرجل أراد أن يوصي وله عيال

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAli stopped a client with seven hundred from making a will, saying that this did not count as wealth under the verse.
rows.anchor: وعن علي: أن مولى له أراد أن يوصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lack of a fixed amount does not negate obligation: the apparent rule applies once any wealth exists; if khayr has a narrower sense, juristic judgment determines what qualifies as good and sufficient wealth.
rows.anchor: ولا يدل عدم تقدير المال على أن الوصية لم تجب، إذ الظاهر التعليق بوجود مطلق الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the estate khayr subtly implies that it is lawful wealth: illicit property must be returned to its owners, and making a will from it is sinful.
rows.anchor: وفي تسميته هنا وجعله خيرا إشارة لطيفة إلى أنه مال طيب لا خبيث

rows.speaker: قول غير مسمى
rows.claim: One view holds the verse operative and makes a bequest to parents and relatives obligatory alongside their inheritance under the two verses.
rows.anchor: فقال قوم: الآية محكمة، والوصية للوالدين والأقربين واجبة

rows.speaker: قول غير مسمى
rows.claim: Another view considers the verse operative but understands it to recommend voluntary bequests.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: إنها محكمة في التطوع

rows.speaker: قول غير مسمى
rows.claim: A further view says the will command does not conflict with inheritance; it concerns God's assignment of parents' and relatives' shares.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: إنها محكمة وليس معنى الوصية مخالفا للميراث، بل المعنى: كتب عليكم ما أوصى به الله

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the person near death must preserve for parents and relatives the shares God assigned them and not reduce those allotments.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: أو كتب على المحتضر أن يوصي للوالدين والأقربين بتوفير ما أوصى به الله لهم عليهم

rows.speaker: الحسن وطاووس والضحاك
rows.claim: They limit the operative command to parents and relatives who do not inherit, such as enslaved or non-Muslim kin, and to a bequest of one third or less.
rows.anchor: قاله الحسن، وطاووس، والضحاك

rows.speaker: ابن المنذر
rows.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir reports a consensus among the scholars known to him that bequests to non-inheriting parents and relatives are permissible.
rows.anchor: وقال: ابن المنذر: أجمع كل من يحفظ عنه من أهل العلم على أن الوصية للوالدين والأقرباء الذين لا يرثون جائزة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: They say the verse initially governed all relatives, then was abrogated as to anyone who inherits by the inheritance verse.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس، والحسن، وقتادة: الآية عامة، وتقرر الحكم بها برهة، ونسخ منها كل من يرث بآية الفرائض

rows.speaker: ابن عمر وابن عباس وابن زيد
rows.claim: They regard the entire verse as abrogated; the bequest remains recommended, a position also attributed to al-Shaʿbi, al-Nakhaʿi, and Malik.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عمر، وابن عباس أيضا، وابن زيد: الآية كلها منسوخة. وبقيت الوصية ندبا

rows.speaker: الربيع بن خثيم وغيره
rows.claim: Al-Rabiʿ ibn Khuthaym and others are reported as holding that there is no bequest.
rows.anchor: لا وصية، وقيل: كانت في بدء الإسلام فنسخت بآية المواريث

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A prophetic report says God has assigned each rightful holder his right and that there is no bequest for an heir; the community's acceptance gives this solitary report near mass-transmitted status because they accept only established sound reports.
rows.anchor: وبقوله عليه السلام: «إن الله أعطى كل ذي حق حقه، ألا لا وصية لوارث»

rows.speaker: قول غير مسمى
rows.claim: One position gives relatives first claim on bequests and bars a bequest to outsiders when relatives are left without one.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: الوصية للقرابة أولا، فإن كانت لأجنبي فمعهم، ولا يجوز لغيرهم مع تركهم

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: When Abu al-ʿAliya left his estate to Banu Hashim despite having been freed by a woman of Riyah, al-Shaʿbi objected that he had no right to do so.
rows.anchor: وقال الشعبي: لم يكن ذلك له ولا كرامة

rows.speaker: طاووس وجابر وابن زيد
rows.claim: They say a bequest to non-relatives is redirected to the testator's relatives and the disposition annulled; this is also related from al-Hasan and held by Ishaq ibn Rahawayh.
rows.anchor: وقال طاووس: إذا أوصى لغير قرابته ردت الوصية إلى قرابته ونقض فعله

rows.speaker: الحسن وجابر بن زيد وعبد الملك بن يعلى
rows.claim: They permit the third of the estate to remain with the recipient the testator selected.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن، وجابر بن زيد، أيضا، وعبد الملك بن يعلى: يبقى ثلث الوصية حيث جعلها الميت

rows.speaker: مالك وأبو حنيفة والشافعي وأحمد
rows.claim: They allow a bequest to an outsider even when relatives are left, whether the recipient is rich or poor and Muslim or non-Muslim; this is also reported from ʿUmar, Ibn ʿAbbas, and ʿAʾisha.
rows.anchor: وقال مالك، وأبو حنيفة، والشافعي، وأحمد: إذا أوصى لغير قرابته وترك قرابته جاز ذلك وأمضي

rows.speaker: الثوري
rows.claim: Al-Thawri takes the apparent command to make a will as obligatory for anyone who leaves property.
rows.anchor: وظاهر: كتب، وجوب الوصية على من خلف مالا، وهو قول الثوري

rows.speaker: أبو ثور
rows.claim: Abu Thawr says a will is obligatory only for someone with a debt or property entrusted by others; it is not obligatory for someone with neither.
rows.anchor: لا تجب إلا على من عليه دين أو عنده مال لقوم، فأما من لا دين عليه

rows.speaker: قول غير مسمى
rows.claim: Another view denies that making a will is obligatory, citing al-Nakhaʿi's report that the Prophet died without making one and a hadith that conditions it on wanting to make a will.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لا تجب الوصية، واستدل بقول النخعي: مات رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ولم يوص

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة ومالك
rows.claim: They permit a bequest to an heir if the other heirs approve it.
rows.anchor: والموصى له، إن كان وارثا وأجاز ذلك الورثة جاز، وبه قال أبو حنيفة، ومالك

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة ومحمد
rows.claim: They allow a bequest to an intentional killer if the heirs approve it; Abu Yusuf says such a bequest is invalid.
rows.anchor: أو قاتلا عمدا وأجاز ذلك الورثة، جاز في قول أبي حنيفة ومحمد. وقال أبو يوسف: لا تجوز

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: If the testator directs that a bequest to an heir go to God's cause unless the heirs approve it, Malik says it becomes part of the estate when they refuse.
rows.anchor: هذا قول مالك

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة ومعمر
rows.claim: They say the refused bequest in that arrangement is spent in God's cause.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة، ومعمر: يمضى في سبيل الله

rows.speaker: ابن أبي ليلى وعثمان البتي
rows.claim: They hold that if heirs approve an outsider's bequest above one third during the testator's life, they cannot revoke that approval after death.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن أبي ليلى، وعثمان البتي

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة ومحمد وأبو يوسف وزفر والحسن بن صالح وعبيد الله بن الحسن
rows.claim: They require heirs to renew their approval after death; consent given during the testator's life alone is ineffective, a view also reported from ʿAbd Allah, Shurayh, and Ibrahim.
rows.anchor: إن أجازوا ذلك في حياته لم يجز ذلك حتى يجيزوه بعد الموت

rows.speaker: ابن القاسم عن مالك
rows.claim: Under Malik's view, separately situated heirs who consent cannot revoke, while dependent household members or close kin may revoke if the testator recovers and can cut off their support.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن القاسم عن مالك: إن استأذنهم فأذنوا فكل وارث بائن فليس له أن يرجع

rows.speaker: ابن وهب عن مالك
rows.claim: Ibn Wahb reports that heirs may withdraw consent given in good health but not consent given during illness; al-Layth agrees with Malik, and jurists agree that approval after death cannot be revoked.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن وهب عن مالك: إن أذنوا له في الصحة فلهم أن يرجعوا، أو في المرض فلا

rows.speaker: طاووس وعطاء
rows.claim: Tawus and ʿAtaʾ hold that heirs' approval during the testator's life is binding.
rows.anchor: وروي عن طاووس وعطاء: إن أجازوه في الحياة جاز عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jurists agree that a sane adult who is not legally interdicted may make a valid will; they disagree about minors: Abu Hanifa bars it, while Malik and others allow it, as do two reported Shafiʿi positions.
rows.anchor: ولا خلاف في صحة وصية العاقل البالغ غير المحجور عليه واختلف في الصبي

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa rejects a minor's will; al-Muzani says this follows by analogy from al-Shafiʿi, while Malik and others permit it.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو حنيفة: لا تجوز وصيته. قال المزني: وهو قياس قول الشافعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command's apparent wording supports barring a minor from making a will because a minor is not legally accountable, but everyone agrees that a person may change or revoke their own will.
rows.anchor: وظاهر قوله تعالى: كتب المنع. لأنه ليس من أهل التكليف، وأجمعوا على أنه للإنسان أن يغير وصيته

rows.speaker: مالك وأبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Malik and Abu Hanifa say an owner cannot revoke a mudabbar arrangement; al-Shafiʿi, Ahmad, Ishaq, al-Shaʿbi, al-Nakhaʿi, Ibn Shubruma, and al-Thawri treat it as a will.
rows.anchor: فذهب مالك وأبو حنيفة إلى أنه ليس له أن يغير ما دبر، قال الشافعي، وأحمد، وإسحاق: هو وصيته

rows.speaker: النبي وعائشة
rows.claim: The Prophet is reported to have sold a mudabbar, and ʿAʾisha sold a female mudabbar; these sales are cited in the dispute over whether the arrangement can be revoked.
rows.anchor: وأن عائشة باعت مدبرة، وإذا قال لعبده

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik allows revocation after the words You are free after my death; saying someone is a mudabbar cannot be revoked, nor can the first wording be retracted if it was intended as manumission after death.
rows.anchor: وإذا قال لعبده: أنت حر بعد موتي، فله الرجوع عند مالك في ذلك

rows.speaker: الشافعي وأحمد وإسحاق وأبو ثور
rows.claim: They classify all these formulations as wills.
rows.anchor: وأما الشافعي، وأحمد، وإسحاق، وأبو ثور، فكل هذا عندهم وصية

rows.speaker: أبو ثور
rows.claim: Abu Thawr says the declaration I have revoked my mudabbar cancels the arrangement; al-Shafiʿi requires an actual sale or gift, since merely saying I revoke is ineffective.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو ثور: إذا قال: رجعت في مدبري بطل التدبير، وقال الشافعي: لا يكون إلا ببيع أو هبة

rows.speaker: ابن القاسم وأشهب
rows.claim: For the ambiguous statement that a slave will be free after the owner's death without expressly intending a will or manumission arrangement, Ibn al-Qasim calls it a will and Ashhab calls it a mudabbar.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن القاسم: هو وصية؟ وقال أشهب: هو مدبر

rows.speaker: الدارقطني عن أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: A testament formula used by the righteous predecessors confesses God's oneness, Muhammad's messengership, the Hour and resurrection, then exhorts one's family to fear God, reconcile, and obey God and His Messenger; it invokes Abraham's and Jacob's counsel to their children to die as Muslims.
rows.anchor: هذا ما أوصى فلان بن فلان، أنه يشهد أن لا إله إلا الله، وحده لا شريك له، وأن محمدا عبده ورسوله

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Al-Daraqutni transmits the cited testament formula from Anas ibn Malik.
rows.anchor: رواه الدارقطني، عن أنس بن مالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kataba is passive, with its agent omitted because God is known to be meant and for brevity; al-waṣiyya is apparently the passive subject, and the feminine verb lacks agreement because of separation, length, nonhuman feminine gender, and the sense of bequeathing.
rows.anchor: وبني كتب للمفعول وحذف الفاعل للعلم به، وللاختصار، إذ معلوم أنه الله تعالى

words: إِذَا حَضَرَ أَحَدَكُمُ ٱلْمَوْتُ إِن تَرَكَ خَيْرًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answers to the two conditions are omitted. The sense is that the will was prescribed for a person when death's signs arrive and, if he has wealth, he should make a will; kataba cannot itself answer because it is past while the conditions are prospective.
rows.anchor: وجواب الشرطين محذوف لدلالة المعنى عليه، ولا يجوز أن يكون من معنى: كتب، لمضي كتب واستقبال الشرطين

words: إِذَا حَضَرَ أَحَدَكُمُ ٱلْمَوْتُ إِن تَرَكَ خَيْرًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second condition has an omitted answer indicated by the first omitted answer, so the omitted answer in turn indicates another omission; the author calls the combined conditional structure one of the hardest syntax problems and refers readers to al-Takmil.
rows.anchor: ويكون جواب الشرط الثاني محذوفا يدل عليه جواب الشرط الأول المحذوف، فيكون المحذوف دل على محذوف

words: كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذَا حَضَرَ أَحَدَكُمُ ٱلْمَوْتُ
rows.speaker: قول غير مسمى
rows.claim: Another parse treats both answers as omitted, understands kataba as future-directed obligation, and makes idha a temporal adverb governed by kataba; the answer to if he leaves wealth is then also omitted and signaled by kataba.
rows.anchor: وقيل: جواب الشرطين محذوف ويقدر من معنى كتب عليكم الوصية ويتجوز بلفظ: كتب

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن
rows.claim: Most grammarians do not let idha be governed by al-waṣiyya because a source or relative cannot have its complement preposed; Abu al-Hasan permits a temporal complement before a non-pure relative/source, as in the cited line attaching bi-l-raḥā to al-mutakāʿis.
rows.anchor: وأجاز ذلك أبو الحسن لأنه يجوز عنده أن يتقدم المعمول إذا كان ظرفا على العامل فيه إذا لم يكن موصولا محضا

words: كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذَا حَضَرَ أَحَدَكُمُ ٱلْمَوْتُ
rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya makes kataba govern idha, takes al-waṣiyya as the passive subject, and supplies a response to both conditions from the preceding kataba; Abū Ḥayyān finds this contradictory because idha cannot be both temporal and conditional.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو محمد بن عطية: ويتجه في إعراب هذه الآية أن يكون: كتب، هو العامل في: إذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya's parse cannot take the earlier spoken kataba as an omitted answer indicated by what precedes; that would make the estimated answer identical to the already uttered word. The apparent parse makes al-waṣiyya the passive subject of kataba.
rows.anchor: وما كان مقدرا يدل عليه ما تقدم يستحيل أن يكون هو الملفوظ به المتقدم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari calls al-waṣiyya the faʿil of kataba, his term for the passive subject, and explains the masculine verb by separation and by the sense of the verbal phrase to make a will.
rows.anchor: قال في تفسيره: والوصية فاعل كتب، وذكر فعلها للفاصل، ولأنها بمعنى: أن يوصي

rows.speaker: قول غير مسمى
rows.claim: Some grammarians make al-waṣiyya a subject in a conditional answer, with an omitted fa or an implied predicate such as it is due; the passive subject would be an implicit yuktabu explained by the wording that follows.
rows.anchor: وأجاز بعض المعربين أن ترتفع الوصية على الابتداء، على تقدير الفاء، والخبر إما محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān again finds Ibn ʿAṭiyya's analysis inconsistent: if idha is governed as a temporal adverb it is not a condition, and an omitted passive subject or unspoken verbal noun cannot serve as the proposed governor under the stated Basran rules.
rows.anchor: لأن الشيء الواحد لا يكون شرطا وغير شرط في حالة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya misquotes Sibawayh's supporting verse; Sibawayh actually cites the line beginning whoever does good deeds, God rewards them, and says this construction is only poetic necessity.
rows.anchor: وأما قوله على نحو ما أيد سيبويه. من يفعل الحسنات الله يحفظه وهو تحريف على سيبويه

rows.speaker: سيبويه عن الخليل
rows.claim: Sibawayh transmits al-Khalil's ruling that a conditional clause without fa, such as if you come to me, I am generous, occurs only when a poet is forced; al-Akhfash's implied-fa analysis is refuted by this evidence.
rows.anchor: قال: لا يكون هذا إلا أن يضطر شاعر من قبل: أن أنا كريم، يكون كلاما مبتدأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The less strained parse makes the prepositional phrase ʿalaykum the passive subject: al-waṣiyya then answers the listener's implicit question about what was prescribed, as subject or predicate.
rows.anchor: وأجاز بعضهم أن تقام مقام المفعول الذي لم يسم فاعله الجار والمجرور الذي هو: عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prepositional phrase serving as passive subject is the best analysis and requires fewer assumptions than positing an implicit verbal noun and its pronoun.
rows.anchor: وهذا الوجه أحسن، وأقل تكلفا من الوجه الذي قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the phrase about parents was discussed earlier in the command to show kindness to parents.
rows.anchor: وتقدم الكلام على ذلك في قوله تعالى: وبالوالدين إحسانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-aqrabīn is the plural of al-aqrab, an elative meaning nearest; its apparent scope includes every relative closer to the deceased, with parents named first and then included again for emphasis and special care.
rows.anchor: والأقربين جمع الأقرب، وظاهره أنه أفعل تفضيل، فكل من كان أقرب إلى الميت دخل في هذا اللفظ

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Exegetes identify the relatives variously as children, relatives other than children, all kin, or non-inheriting relatives.
rows.anchor: وعند المفسرين: الأقربون الأولاد، أو من عدا الأولاد، أو جميع القرابات، أو من لا يرث من الأقارب

rows.speaker: قول غير مسمى
rows.claim: One explanation of fairness limits a bequest to one third and says not to favor the rich over the poor.
rows.anchor: بالمعروف أي: لا يوصي بأزيد من الثلث، ولا للغني دون الفقير

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud explains fairness as giving first to the neediest relative.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود: الأخل فالأخل، أي: الأحوج فالأحوج

rows.speaker: قول غير مسمى
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the will must contain no injustice.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الذي لا حيف فيه

rows.speaker: قول غير مسمى
rows.claim: Another view initially leaves the amount to the testator's judgment, then sets the upper limit at one third, citing the report that one third is much.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كان هذا موكولا إلى اجتهاد الموصي، ثم بين ذلك وقدر

rows.speaker: قول غير مسمى
rows.claim: Fairness may mean a moderate amount recognized by people's conscience without harming heirs, since people had sometimes bequeathed all their property.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بالقصد الذي تعرفه النفوس دون إضرار بالورثة

rows.speaker: قول غير مسمى
rows.claim: Another interpretation requires that the bequest concern a known portion of the testator's property rather than an unspecified amount.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بالمعروف من ماله غير المجهول

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari summarizes fairness as justice: do not leave the poor for the rich and do not exceed one third.
rows.anchor: وقد لخص ذلك الزمخشري وفسره بالعدل، وهو أن لا يوصي للغني ويدع الفقير، ولا يتجاوز الثلث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase bi-l-maʿrūf attaches either to al-waṣiyya or to an omitted adjective meaning characterized by fairness, making it a circumstantial phrase.
rows.anchor: وتعلق بالمعروف بقوله: الوصية، أو بمحذوف، أي: كائنة بالمعروف، فيكون بالمعروف حالا من الوصية

rows.speaker: ابن عطية والزمخشري
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya and al-Zamakhshari parse ḥaqqan as an emphatic verbal noun affirming the sentence's content, roughly this is truly binding.
rows.anchor: انتصب: حقا، على أنه مصدر مؤكد لمضمون الجملة، أي: حق ذلك حقا، قاله ابن عطية، والزمخشري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects that parse because the following phrase ʿalā al-muttaqīn must attach to ḥaqqan or describe it, which prevents ḥaqqan from being an emphatic verbal noun under the grammatical rules he cites.
rows.anchor: وهذا تأباه القواعد النحوية لأن ظاهر قوله: على المتقين إذن يتعلق على ب: حقا

rows.speaker: قول غير مسمى
rows.claim: The pronoun in heard it may refer to the act of bequeathing, to God's command in the verse, or the pronoun in changed it may refer to the prescribed obligation and ruling.
rows.anchor: والضمير في سمعه عائد على الإيصاء كما شرحناه، وقيل: يعود على أمر الله تعالى في هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional whoever is general, covering anyone who changes the will by rewriting it, reallocating rights, giving false testimony, concealing testimony, or otherwise preventing property from reaching its rightful owner.
rows.anchor: ومن: الظاهر أنها شرطية، والجواب: فإنما إثمه وتكون: من، عامة في كل مبدل

rows.speaker: قول غير مسمى
rows.claim: One interpretation restricts whoever to the executor, who controls fairness, bias, alteration, and implementation.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المراد بمن: متولي الإيصاء دون الموصي والموصى له

rows.speaker: قول غير مسمى
rows.claim: Another interpretation means the testator himself, forbidden to divert the will from the relatives God named toward outsiders; on this reading both pronouns refer to God's command.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المراد: بمن: هو الموصي، نهي عن تغيير وصيته عن المواضع التي نهى الله عن الوصية إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hearing stands for knowledge, since it is the means by which the command is learned; a changer incurs sin only if they knew the command.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله: بعد ما سمعه دليل على أن الإثم لا يترتب إلا بشرط أن يكون المبدل قد علم بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its pronoun refers either to the altered will or to the verbal noun implied by changed it, meaning the sin of alteration; the passage shows that a sinner bears their own penalty, not the deceased, if an executor fails.
rows.anchor: فإنما إثمه: الضمير عائد على الإيصاء المبدل، أو على المصدر المفهوم من بدله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer names those who change the will instead of using a pronoun, highlighting alteration as the cause of the sin; the relative clause uses the future form by default.
rows.anchor: وراعى المعنى في قوله: على الذين يبدلونه إذ لو جرى على نسق اللفظ الأول لكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing attributes threaten the changers: God knows nothing is hidden and will punish the alteration. Other explanations say He hears the testator or his wills and knows the executor's acts or intentions; the author prefers the first because the phrase follows mention of alteration and its sin.
rows.anchor: والظاهر القول الأول لمجيئه في أثر ذكر التبديل وما يترتب عليه من الإثم
